name: sleep
_thoughts: before sleeping: how tired you are (energy, same bands as the bar), then up to 3 things you remember from today, most memorable first

text: You lie down, too exhausted to think.
You fall down where you are. You can't keep your eyes open.
Your legs give way. Too tired to care.
You lie down. Every muscle aches.
You lie down. Everything hurts.
You curl up, aching all over.
You lie down, tired in a slow, heavy way.
You stretch out. A slow tiredness comes over you.
You lie down, heavy and tired.
You lie down, not really tired. Sleep is slow to come.
You lie down and close your eyes. Sleep takes its time.
You are not tired. You lie down and wait for sleep.

intro: The day comes back to you in pieces.
Pieces of the day drift back.
You think back over the day.
Lying still, you go over the day.
In the quiet, the day replays.
Before sleep, the day returns to you.

text: The cold sea. Waking alone on the sand.
The shock of waking on the beach, alone.
Salt, cold, and no ship on the horizon.
Carving the spear with the knife, shaving by shaving.
The knife turning a branch into a spear.
The spear you carved, its point sharp under your thumb.
Hacking at a branch with the rock knife until it had a point.
The blunt rock knife, and the spear it made, slowly.
A spear made with a blade of stone.
Grinding a stone into a blade, for hours.
Stone on stone, until it had an edge.
The rock knife, and how long it took.
Fish flashing in the shallows, just out of reach.
Silver fish in the shallows, too quick to catch.
The fish in the shallows, so close.
Building the shelter, log by log.
The shelter against the rocks, and how still it is inside.
The wind breaking on the logs you raised.
The first harvest from the field.
Breaking the corn off the stalks.
Arms full of corn.
Hacking at the wood with the axe.
The axe biting into wood.
Logs, real logs, at last.
Standing in the surf with the spear raised.
Cold water to your knees, the spear ready.
Waiting in the surf for the fish to come close.
The view from the cliff top: grass all the way inland.
The wind at the top of the cliff, and the meadows below.
Climbing the cliff, and the green land behind it.
A clear river under the willows.
The river, cold and quick over the stones.
Fish holding still in the river's slow pools.
Wading in the river with the spear raised.
The river pulling at your legs while you waited for a fish.
Fishing in the slow pools under the willows.
A match flaring in your cupped hands, then warmth.
One match, and the fire took.
The smell of a struck match, then woodsmoke.
Wood against wood until your palms burned, and at last a flame.
Hours of rubbing sticks before the fire came.
Your raw palms, and the first ember.
Striking stone on stone until a spark held.
Sparks in the tinder, and at last a flame.
Your sore knuckles, and the fire the stones made.
Cold water from a spring between mossy stones.
The spring, and how cold the water was.
Drinking from the spring until your teeth ached.
A ring of rocks, out of the wind.
The ring of rocks where the wind can't reach.
Shelter among the rocks.
The cool dark under the trees.
The forest, quiet and dim.
Tall trunks and the smell of moss.
Long grass, and the wind moving through it.
The open meadows under a wide sky.
Grass to the knee, silver in the wind.
Purple fingers from the berries.
Picking berries, thorns in your sleeves.
The sour, sweet taste of the berries.
The smell of food over the fire.
Food cooking on the hot stones.
The smell of something cooking.
Armful after armful of dry branches.
Dragging dry branches out of the forest.
Bark and twigs, scratching your arms.
Shells pried from the wet stone.
Cold fingers on wet shells.
Shells, and the surf soaking your legs.
The taste of fresh water.
Water, at last.
Cold, clean water.
Something in your stomach, at least.
Food, of a kind.
You ate. That is something.

otherwise: A day of small things. You hardly remember it.
The day blurs. Nothing stands out.
Little to remember. Sand, waiting, more sand.
thoughts._lines: most memorable first; the fire and the spear are remembered the way you did them (matches, stones or friction; knife or rock knife)

_afterwards: the night itself is quiet; on waking: the engine announces the new day and sleep quality, then one line on how your body is (worst first), then the fire

text: Your body is weak and shaking. The night took something from you.
You are weak. Your hands won't stop shaking.
You can barely sit up. The night was hard on you.
Hunger and thirst, both at once.
Your stomach aches and your mouth is dry.
Hungry, thirsty, both.
Your mouth is dry, your tongue thick.
Your throat is dry as sand.
Thirst wakes you before the light does.
Your stomach is a hollow ache.
Hunger, first thing.
Your belly is empty and loud.
You are stiff with cold.
The cold has got into your joints.
You wake shivering.
You feel rested.
You feel stronger.
Rested, for once.
You are still tired.
Tired still, though you slept.
The sleep did little.
The fire still smoulders in the ring of rocks.
Embers still glow in the rocks.
A little smoke still rises from the fire.
The fire is long out. Only cold ash.
Cold ash where the fire was.
The fire is gone. Not even smoke.
The fire died in the night.
Sometime in the night, the fire went out.
The fire did not last the night.
